I'd go with the first version — the one that keeps it archived unless I say otherwise. Both handled the important part correctly: neither made a second copy. Pasting the link again just took me to the one I already had, even though it was tucked away in the archive, which is the no-duplicates behavior I've wanted all along.

The reason I prefer the first one is that archiving something was a deliberate choice I made to get it out of my everyday view. If I happen to paste that link again later, that doesn't necessarily mean I want it hauled back out — maybe I'm just checking, or I forgot I'd archived it. The first version respects that: it clearly tells me "this one's archived," lets me make my edits right there if I want, and leaves bringing it back as a button I press on purpose. The second version quietly restored it to my collection just because I re-added it, and that could surprise me by cluttering my main list back up with something I'd intentionally set aside.

So: recognize it's the same already-saved page, tell me plainly it's in the archive, and let me decide whether to restore it rather than doing it for me. That's the safer, more natural one.
